plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that produces fragrant, five-petaled blossoms on bare branches before its leaves emerge. It is widely cultivated in Japan, China, and Korea, where it is prized as a harbinger of spring and often grown as bonsai.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (February to March)
plants.location: East Asia (Japan, China, Korea); cultivated worldwide in temperate gardens
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms bloom while snow may still be on the ground, so they symbolize perseverance and hope in East Asian culture. The fruit is pickled to make umeboshi and used to flavor umeshu liqueur.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with trumpet-shaped yellow flowers surrounded by paler outer petals. It carpets woodlands, meadows, and gardens across western Europe, and countless cultivars are grown in gardens elsewhere.
plants.location: Western Europe (UK, France, Spain); naturalized in North America and cultivated in temperate regions worldwide
plants.funFact: Daffodils contain lycorine and galantamine. Galantamine is extracted from related Narcissus and Galanthus species and used in medicine to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A large evergreen shrub with giant, bowl-shaped flower heads made of colorful bracts surrounding a central cluster of true flowers. It grows in the fynbos vegetation of South Africa and is a popular cut flower.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to early autumn in the Southern Hemisphere, with flowering from about February to May in some populations
plants.location: Western and Southern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower. Proteas are an ancient plant lineage that predates the breakup of Gondwana, and the flower heads can reach 30 cm across.

plants.name: Magnolia campbellii
plants.description: A towering deciduous tree from the Himalayas that bears huge, goblet-shaped, fragrant flowers on bare branches. It is grown in mild, moist gardens in Britain, New Zealand, and the Pacific Northwest.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (February to April)
plants.location: Himalayan foothills (Nepal, Bhutan, Sikkim, Yunnan); cultivated in mild temperate gardens
plants.funFact: Magnolia trees are among the oldest flowering plants. Their flowers evolved before bees existed and are adapted to pollination by beetles, and a Campbell's magnolia may take 20 or more years from seed to flower.
